Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals · Section 15.7 · Exercise 17

A Triple Integral over the Solid between a Paraboloid and a Plane

Problem

Evaluate the triple integral

∭E​xdV,

where the solid E is bounded by the paraboloid x=4y2+4z2 and the plane x=4.

Reading the solid

The two surfaces meet on the curve where both equations hold, that is, where 4y2+4z2=4. Divide by 4 to obtain the circle y2+z2=1. The solid therefore projects onto the unit disk D={(y,z):y2+z2≤1} in the yz-plane.

At a fixed point (y,z) of D, the x-coordinate runs from the paraboloid to the plane:

4y2+4z2≤x≤4.

Use polar coordinates in the yz-plane, y=rcosθ and z=rsinθ, so that y2+z2=r2. The area element of the disk is dA=rdrdθ, hence

dV=dxdA=rdxdrdθ.

In these coordinates the solid is described by the simple inequalities

4r2≤x≤4,0≤r≤1,0≤θ≤2π.

Solution

Step 1 — Set up the iterated integral

Insert the description of E and the volume element into the triple integral:

∭E​xdV=∫02π​∫01​∫4r24​x⋅rdxdrdθ.

Step 2 — Integrate with respect to x

The variable r is constant during the innermost integration, so

∫4r24​xrdx=r[2x2​]4r24​=2r​(16−16r4)=8r(1−r4).

Step 3 — Integrate over the disk

The inner result depends only on r. Integrate it over 0≤r≤1:

∫01​8r(1−r4)dr=8∫01​(r−r5)dr=8[2r2​−6r6​]01​=8(21​−61​)=8⋅31​=38​.

Step 4 — Integrate with respect to θ

The integrand no longer depends on θ, so the outer integral only multiplies the result by 2π:

∭E​xdV=∫02π​38​dθ=38​⋅2π=316π​.

Answer

∭E​xdV=316π​≈16.755.

Notation

SymbolMeaning
∭E​fdVThe triple integral of the function f over the three-dimensional region E; it is the limit of sums of f times small volumes.
EThe solid region of integration, that is, the set of points that satisfy the stated inequalities.
dVThe volume element. In Cartesian coordinates dV=dxdydz; in the polar coordinates used here dV=rdxdrdθ.
x=4y2+4z2A parabolic bowl (an elliptic paraboloid) that opens along the positive x-axis.
r,θPolar coordinates in the yz-plane: r is the distance from the x-axis and θ is the angle around it.
the factor rThe Jacobian factor of polar coordinates. A small polar rectangle has area rdrdθ, not drdθ.
DThe projection of E onto the yz-plane, here the unit disk.
πThe ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, π≈3.14159.

Verification

Three independent computations support the result.

  • part1_step1.py checks the region description and estimates the integral by Monte Carlo sampling; the estimate is 16.746, within one standard error of 16π/3=16.755.
  • part1_step2.py repeats the symbolic evaluation with SymPy and obtains 16π/3.
  • part1_step3.py evaluates the integral numerically with mpmath in two different orders of integration, and both values agree with 16π/3 to twelve digits.
